text:
maria (support): Customer reporting intermittent 502/504s on Hosted API when sending large parallel embed batches. Started ~2026-03-14T09:12:xxZ, spike at ~09:18. They see early connection closes from the gateway. sample request id: rq_3f7a9b38. They attached a curl repro but asked us to triage.

todd (eng-sre): can you paste the minimal curl they used + one failing trace id? I want to check envoy downstream logs and stream state.

maria (support): pasted curl below (customer redacted tokens):

curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer ***" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -d '{"model":"rwd-embed-xxl","inputs":["...lots of texts..." ]}'

also they included this trace header: x-rw-trace: tr_0a1b2c3d

lee (eng-infra): quick snapshot from edge metrics around 09:15-09:22UTC: h2_active_streams per frontdoor node spiked to ~310 (threshold is 256), conn_reset_rate upstream increased, downstream tcp FIN/ACK count rose.

lee (eng-infra): paste of the specific metric lines:

```
frontdoor-node-7.h2_active_streams = 312
frontdoor-node-7.conn_resets_per_min = 42
upstream-hosts/embeds-pool/active_conns = 12
```

sanjay (eng-platform): that h2_active_streams > 256 is suspicious — Envoy default max concurrent streams per connection is 256 on many clients. If one client holds a lot of streams and then closes, we can get RST/early-close cascades that look like 502 from the gateway.

ben (eng-runtime): also looking at our gateway logs for rq_3f7a9b38: envoy reported "stream reset, code: REFUSED_STREAM" followed by upstream idle connection closed. We saw a burst of REFUSED_STREAM and early closures. Could be client-side churn + keepalive mismatch.

maria (support): customer says they run 50 parallel workers hitting embeddings with batches of ~128 texts each. We asked them to reduce to 8 and test; they said the errors drop but latency increases.

todd (eng-sre): repro plan: run local load test with 50 concurrent HTTP/2 streams over a single connection simulating their batching. capture envoy downstream logs + tcpdump on frontdoor node. also capture x-rw-trace header when failure occurs.

sanjay (eng-platform): suggested quick mitigation for customer: throttle concurrency from client side to <= 16, or use multiple client connections spread across hosts (HTTP/1.1 or multiple HTTP/2 connections). We can also temporarily route them to Dedicated pool if they have a contract.

lee (eng-infra): config changes to test internally: increase envoy upstream max_concurrent_streams to 512 for a small subset of nodes, and add additional keepalive probing to detect half-closed connections earlier. Will roll to canary nodes.

ben (eng-runtime): NOTE: changing max_concurrent_streams has cost/risk — could let single tenant occupy connection too long. prefer targeted mitigation + client-side throttling first.

maria (support): infra-bot created ticket INC-20260314-47 and attached initial logs. @todd assigned.

infra-bot: [incident created] INC-20260314-47 - edge gateway REFUSED_STREAM spike - severity P2

todd (eng-sre): next steps:
- capture pcap from frontdoor-node-7 for 09:10-09:25
- collect envoy access + error logs for trace tr_0a1b2c3d and rq_3f7a9b38
- ask customer to run this quick curl that sets multiple connections instead of single conn:

curl -H "Connection: keep-alive" -H "X-RW-TRACE: tr_0a1b2c3d" --limit-rate 10k ...

maria (support): I already asked customer to run reduced concurrency test; they confirmed fewer errors. I sent them the multi-conn curl and asked for a failing request id if it still happens.

sanjay (eng-platform): if we can reproduce, capture these logs:
- envoy config dump (listeners/clusters)
- envoy stats for h2_active_streams and reset_reason
- firehose traces (x-rw-trace)

ben (eng-runtime): also consider adding a temporary rule to detect a single source pinning too many streams and return 429 early. That'll be a short-term throttle to protect shared frontdoor.

maria (support): customer okay with a brief throttle, they prefer uptime over raw throughput. I can enable a per-IP soft throttle if we want to test.

lee (eng-infra): canary change pushed to 3 nodes to increase concurrent streams limit and enable more aggressive idle probe. Monitoring dashboards updated.

todd (eng-sre): keep an eye on REFUSED_STREAM and connection reset counts. If increase fixes errors without downstream overload, we can rollback throttle.

maria (support): I'll keep customer updated. thanks everyone — assigning followups in INC-20260314-47. Will post final resolution here.

ben (eng-runtime): quick note — add a log line to include "client_connection_id" and active_streams count on envoys that log REFUSED_STREAM; will help debug further.

maria (support): noted. closing loop: customer saw 80% reduction after client throttling. infra will continue canary and we'll decide on permanent config next week. :thumbsup:
